capability_reduction.reason: DRAM per die under the stage-8 default (combo_a_kv): the advertised 1,048,576 tokens need 1,048,576 x 6,336 B = 6.64 GB of replicated DSA cache per die, against 3.05 GB free after the weights load (before the 64 MiB trace region and the measured 1,024 MiB workspace). This is a limit of the current replicated cache layout and workspace, not a hard device limit: path_to_advertised lists the layouts that raise it

capability_reduction.path_to_advertised: Measured layouts: replicated fp8 latent (stage-8 default, 6,336 B/token/die): 311,296 tokens at 1 slot; block-sharded bf16 latent (MCOpts.dsa_shard, GLM53_PRECISION=none only, 3,696 B/token/die): 281,344 at 1 slot (stage 4, 900 MiB workspace; ~338K estimated at a 700 MiB workspace, not re-probed: the fp8 replicated default supersedes it as the serving layout). Remaining headroom, byte math per die: (a) pool-key sharding on top of the block-sharded bf16 latent: 11 x (544 x 2 / 4 + 64 / 4) = 3,168 B/token (+16.7 % over 3,696); not implemented: needs a distributed indexer top-512 (per-die pool-key scores, a candidate all-gather and a second top-k with a tie-break identical to the replicated selection, plus owner-die-only pool-key writes in the open-pool update) -- a decoder change of the stage-4/5 path, worth ~+50K tokens; (b) block-sharded fp8 latent: 11 x (544 / 4 + 64) = 2,200 B/token (~1.6x the fp8 replicated capacity): blocked by the shard merge's control columns (the KILL logit -1e4 overflows fp8 e4m3, max 448; the sink / ONE columns need an exact 1.0) -- a stage-8 / stage-4 item with an accuracy gate (TF top-5 >= 98 %, long-context copy); (c) host embedding lookup frees ~317 MB per die but breaks the on-device token-feedback decode contract (split sampling writes the token into the device token buffer): not an option. Even (a)+(b) stay below 1,048,576 (1M x 2,200 B = 2.3 GB per die > the ~1.8 GB available after weights and the reserve).
